draft.title: Inverse proportion
card: In inverse proportion, \(y = \frac{k}{x}\), where \(k\) is a fixed number called the constant. As \(x\) gets bigger, \(y\) gets smaller.
Doubling \(x\) halves \(y\). Tripling \(x\) divides \(y\) by 3. The product \(x \times y\) always equals \(k\).
The graph is a curve called a hyperbola. It never touches either axis.
Example: a 120 km trip takes \(t = \frac{120}{s}\) hours at a speed of \(s\) km/h. At 60 km/h, \(t = 120 \div 60 = 2\) hours. At 120 km/h, \(t = 1\) hour. Doubling the speed halved the time.

4.alt: The curve \(t = \frac{120}{s}\), time in hours against speed in km/h for a 120 km trip. It falls as the speed rises and never touches either axis. It passes through \((60, 2)\) and \((120, 1)\): doubling the speed halves the time.

draft.remember: When \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\), \(y = \frac{k}{x}\) and \(x \times y\) stays the same, so when one doubles the other halves.

a.q: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\). When \(x = 4\), \(y = 12\). Find \(y\) when \(x = 8\).
a.why: Here \(k = x \times y = 4 \times 12 = 48\), so \(y = \frac{48}{8} = 6\). Doubling \(x\) halves \(y\). The answer 24 comes from doubling \(y\), which treats the relationship as direct rather than inverse.

b.q: A trip of 240 km takes Leila 3 hours at an average of 80 km/h. How long does it take at an average of 60 km/h?
b.why: \(\text{Time} = \frac{240}{\text{speed}}\), so \(t = 240 \div 60 = 4\) hours. Check: \(80 \times 3 = 240\) and \(60 \times 4 = 240\), so the product stays the same. Slower speed means more time, so 2.25 hours is wrong. That answer comes from multiplying 3 by \(\frac{60}{80}\), which treats the relationship as direct.
b.clue: Distance stays 240 km, so \(\text{speed} \times \text{time}\) stays the same.
